statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend closure of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window. Stress remains in the elevated band because the long-end rate, energy-corridor and diplomatic questions behind it are unresolved, not because any drawdown was observed.
recommendation: Tail stays far below the block threshold in every published hour: no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, fifteen hours beyond the final slot. Stress describes a 5.18% 10-year, $92.41 WTI and a reported rejection of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 remains inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail holds at its halt floor while a 5.18% 10-year, $92 crude and a reported rejection of Iran's Hormuz plan keep Stress in the elevated band
body: Every Nasdaq-100 venue has been shut since the Friday 21:00Z settle, and the whole 24-hour published window closes fifteen hours before CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday. Friday's session was orderly and two-sided: cash NDX closed 30,608.14, up 129.28 points or 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, against a 30,478.86 previous close. December NQ futures settled 30,889.25, +0.40%, in a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, and VIX closed 14.87, -5.11%, inside 14.68-15.94. None of the inherited Tail amplifiers were present at the settle: retracements occurred repeatedly, no session extreme was held into the bell, and there was no repeated extension after a failed pullback. Tail therefore sits at 8, its halt floor, for the current hour and stays between 7 and 8 across the window, because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path and none can exist before the reopen. Stress at 47 stays in the elevated band on unresolved conditions rather than observed losses. The H.15 September 24 column puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, the highest long-end readings since the financial-crisis era, and Friday reporting described the market as shrugging off that bond move rather than resolving it. WTI eased 2.33% to $92.41 on optimism about a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; that optimism has since been undercut by reporting that Iran's seven-day proposal was rejected, with the waterway still heavily restricted. This is a Sunday-reopen repricing question, not a present one, and it is treated as conditional throughout the forecast. Shared Finviz context was read and is partial: its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, while breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were present as explicitly latest-session, non-real-time data showing six of eight megacaps higher with META -3.33%, and a mixed-positive chip tape with QCOM +3.97% against INTC -3.45%. That context was used only as confirmation and never as evidence of live structure. Confidence opens at 84 on verified index, futures, volatility, yield, energy and calendar evidence, then decays to 78 by the final slot as the Friday reference ages toward 35 hours without a refreshing tick. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a danger window inside a closed tape would be meaningless; the next week's checkpoints, August PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM manufacturing on Thursday, September payrolls on Friday and Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter report after Wednesday's close, all fall outside this window and are carried as conditional drivers.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 8 and 22 and never reached the block threshold. The September 25 European and US cash stretch from 08:00Z to 14:00Z produced two trend-up prints and a run of WATCH states at Tail 19-22 as the index worked higher; the 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. From 15:00Z the state returned to EA_ON at Tail 18-19 in a mixed mode, and after the 21:00Z futures settle it stepped down through Tail 12 to a stable 8-10 on a normal mode for the whole overnight closure. Stress fell from the mid-50s to the mid-40s over the same stretch while Confidence held between 82 and 88.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, fifteen hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 8 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers - shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or the index holding near an extreme - can be observed while every venue is shut. Every hour therefore maps to EA_ON and green. Stress eases from 47 toward 44 through the Saturday hours as Friday's two-sided evidence ages without contradiction, then returns to 47 into Sunday morning as the window tilts conditionally toward an unresolved reopen backdrop of post-crisis long-end yields, a restricted Hormuz corridor and a rejected Iranian proposal. Confidence declines from 84 to 78 purely with evidence age. No danger window is published, and the reopening auction itself falls outside this window.
